title: The Still Swimming Pool
premise_public: At a busy indoor swimming pool, a lifeguard stopped practice because the surface had become unusually still. The pump motor was audibly running, the water looked clear, and no swimmer felt ill.
solution_summary: Debris had blocked the pool pump's intake strainer, so its motor continued running but little water moved through the system. With no flow, the return jets stopped making ripples and the flow-dependent disinfectant feeder shut off. The lifeguard recognized the lack of circulation and cleared the pool before the water became unsafe.

facts.text: A blockage in the pump's intake strainer prevented normal water flow.
The pump motor could run audibly without actually circulating enough water.
The return jets were no longer producing their normal surface ripples.
A safety interlock stopped disinfectant dosing when water flow fell too low.
The lifeguard cleared swimmers as a preventive water-quality measure.
The water could still look clear shortly after circulation stopped.

acceptable_solutions: The pump intake was blocked, so the motor ran without circulating water and the disinfectant feeder stopped, prompting evacuation.
Debris clogged the pump strainer and stopped the return jets; the lifeguard cleared the pool because filtration and dosing were not working.
The motor was on but there was no circulation due to a blockage, so the flow-linked disinfectant system shut down and everyone had to leave.
hints: Hearing machinery run does not prove it is doing its job.
Ask what should be moving through the equipment and what relies on that movement.
